text: Everything from the requirement through the publish exists to support a few minutes of conversation inside the pricing review. That conversation is where this project either lands or doesn't.

The biggest mistake in presenting any dashboard is walking through it visual by visual, top to bottom, narrating what each one is before saying what it means. For a meeting already covering pricing across the whole catalog, that's backwards. Lead with the answer instead.

A simple three-beat structure covers it. First, the headline, ten to fifteen seconds -- the KPI cards, stated as a sentence. Second, the why, thirty to forty-five seconds -- the bar chart, showing which categories are driving or dragging that headline number. Third, the detail, only if someone actually asks -- the table, not narrated by default.

Said out loud, the headline sounds like this: overall this quarter, Bikes and Components are carrying most of our sales, while Clothing is running fewer, smaller orders than the other categories. That's said before pointing at anything on the screen.

And since a category slicer exists, use it live -- click a specific category and let the room watch the cards and chart update, rather than just describing that it can. When someone asks something out of scope, like a year-over-year comparison, the right answer is short and honest: not in this version, happy to add it as a follow-up -- not a guess, and not a long apology.
With the presentation delivered, the last lesson recaps everything this project actually built, and where the Intermediate project picks up.
